fields.rt-blog-html:
The time has come to equip yourself with a cash register system or to replace the solution you opted for in the past? In addition to being efficient and adapted to your expectations, it must above all comply with the law. It must therefore be certified by the software publisher itself or, even better, meet the NF525 standard.

No need to frown. By the end of this article, you'll know everything there is to know about this government certification!

‍

1. Cash Registers in Restaurants: What Are the Legal Requirements?

Finance Law No. 2015-1785 of December 29, 2015—and more specifically, Article 88 of the so-called “anti-VAT fraud” law—establishes the legal and regulatory framework governing cash register systems. As a restaurant owner, you are under no obligation to install a cash register, but if you do, it must comply with this law, effective February 1, 2018.  

This law obliges each professional who owns a cash register and is subject to VAT to obtain a certificate of conformity. This certification can take two different forms. 

The first, and without a doubt the simplest and most effective, is the NF525 certification. Before being a standard, NF is above all a mark owned by the AFNOR group. The NF525 mark, which is the subject of this article, is managed by INFOCERT on behalf of AFNOR. By granting this certification, this accredited organization allows cash register and payment systems editors to offer merchants and restaurant owners solutions that guarantee data reliability and integrity. 

The second option was an individual certificate issued directly by the software publisher. As of September 1, 2025, this self-certification system is no longer accepted. From now on, only a certificate issued by an accredited body—Infocert/AFNOR for NF525, or the LNE—is recognized by the tax authorities.

What are these conditions? Find out in the next paragraph. You’ll also need to agree to the terms and sign the document with your software provider. While this self-certification system is fully compliant from a legal standpoint, restaurant owners who use the point-of-sale software have less protection in the event of an inspection.

‍

2. What does the NF525 standard specify? 

The NF525 certification aims to prove that your cash register system meets the following conditions: 

  • Condition of security : the software used must allow to secure the original data, all the modifications made as well as the supporting documents. 
  • Condition of inalterability : the software used preserves all the data without possibility of return or modification. Similarly, all corrections must be written down.
  • Archiving conditions : the software must provide for an archiving period where the data is frozen and dated with a technical device guaranteeing the integrity of the information.
  • Retention conditions: the software must keep the data for a minimum of 6 years and close them at regular intervals.

These 4 conditions are intended to prevent the modification or deletion of data, a maneuver put in place to reduce the taxation applied to the restaurant.

Your software or cash register system must also comply with the ISO 9001 standard for quality requirements, especially for customer satisfaction .

Beyond the legal obligation, this certification is also a plus for the daily management of your activity since it will considerably facilitate the follow-up and analysis of orders. It is also a competitive advantage and strengthens the confidence of your customers.

‍

3. How can you identify an NF525 certificate? 

The NF525 certificate takes the form of an A4 document and includes the following information:

  • the certificate number,
  • the date,
  • the name and address of your establishment,
  • the name of the software and its version,
  • the name of the certifying body,
  • and the validity date of the certificate.

In the event of an audit, this is the document that will be required. You can find it online or your publisher will send it to you upon request.

To find out whether a software publisher is certified or not, simply visit the NF525 website and search for the product or publisher name. After that, there’s no room for doubt!

‍

4. What are the risks of noncompliance?

In the event of an inspection, your only obligation as a restaurant owner is to provide the Directorate General of Public Finances (DGFiP) with the certificate of compliance issued by an accredited body (Infocert/AFNOR for NF525, or the LNE). The fine for non-compliance is 7,500 euros.

Following the tax authorities' inspection, you will then have 60 days to submit your certificate or face a second fine of a similar amount. Penalties are also applied until the day of compliance.

Please note that within 30 days of receiving the fine, restaurant owners may make representations or submit a valid certificate of compliance. If the proof requested by the administration is provided within this time frame, then the fine may be cancelled.

Finally, the submission of a false certificate is a crime punishable by 3 years in prison and a fine of 45,000 euros. 

‍

5. Which cash register should you choose?

The Innovorder touchscreen cash register, of course!

The cash register that we offer is certified NF525.

The proof is right here: our certificate!  

Spoiler Alert: Our payment processing system not only complies with current regulations, but—more importantly—it’s integrated with all the solutions we offer! 

Thanks to its touch screen, our cash register is both intuitive and scalable and will allow you to manage your omnichannel sales with ease so that you can focus on the essential: customer satisfaction.

👉 To go further: discover Charlene's testimonial, BCHEF franchisee.

At Innovorder, we consider the cash register to be the conductor of your restaurant. That's why it's so important to choose it carefully!

The one that we put at your disposal allows you to :

  • Receive all your orders, regardless of the channel used (counter, kiosk, online order, table order via QR code, click and collect, etc.)
  • centralize the management of the peripherals with which your restaurant is equipped : POS, order terminal, coin dispenser, printer, beeper, cash drawer, etc.

Our cash register is also a great management tool because it facilitates the analysis of your data and allows you to make accurate reports of your activity to make the right decisions.

👉 Learn more: Guide: Which cash register should you choose for your restaurant?

‍

NF525 compliance timetable: what you need to know

To support publishers and merchants in the transition to the new tax certification requirements, the French tax authorities have defined a three-stage timetable, with proof of compliance varying from period to period.

Phase 1: February 16 to August 31, 2025

During this initial transitional phase, companies have several ways of certifying the compliance of their software:

  • An official certificate issued by an accredited body (such as NF525 or LNE),
  • Proof of commitment to an audit (signed quotation, current contract or order with a certifier),
  • A certificate of conformity supplied directly by the software publisher.

This period is intended to give market players the time they need to begin their compliance process.

👉 To find out more: NF525 or LNE: which certification for your cash register?

Phase 2: September 1, 2025, to August 31, 2026

From September onwards, the rules will become stricter. The certificate provided by the publisher will no longer be sufficient. Two documents will be accepted:

  • The official certificate of conformity,
  • Or proof of involvement in a current audit.

Phase 3: from September 1, 2026

Starting in September 2026, only an official NF525 or LNE certificate will be accepted. No other documentation, including letters of commitment, will be accepted.
